# CloudFront Origins

## Overview

When you create a distribution, you specify the origin where CloudFront sends requests for files. CloudFront supports several kinds of origins, including S3 buckets, MediaStore containers, MediaPackage channels, Application Load Balancers, and Lambda function URLs. CloudFront automatically configures most distribution settings based on the content origin type.

An Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer, or EC2 instance in a private subnet can be used as a VPC origin. VPC origins prevent the application from being accessible on the public internet. CloudFront Functions or Lambda@Edge can route requests to different origins based on viewer location, request headers, or query string parameters.

CloudFront uses UTC for signed URLs, signed cookies, logs, and reports.

## Amazon S3 buckets

Using an existing S3 bucket as a CloudFront origin does not change the bucket. You incur regular Amazon S3 charges for storing objects in the bucket. The bucket name must conform to DNS naming requirements to work with CloudFront.

The recommended S3 origin format is bucket-name.s3.region.amazonaws.com. With this format, CloudFront can communicate with the bucket using SSL/TLS, origin access control can require viewers to use CloudFront URLs rather than S3 URLs, and you can update bucket content by sending POST and PUT requests to CloudFront. You should not specify the S3 origin using path style or an S3 CNAME.

CloudFront supports S3 origins in any storage class, including S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which does not impact the performance or functionality of a distribution.

CloudFront data transfer costs less than S3 data transfer at higher usage, and downloads are faster with CloudFront than with S3 alone. To respect S3 CORS settings, CloudFront must forward the Origin header to S3.

### Adding CloudFront to an existing bucket

CloudFront can be added to a bucket already served via your own domain name with no disruption. When you add CloudFront to an existing bucket, a distribution is created with the S3 bucket specified as origin server.

For S3 CNAMEs to work, the DNS provider must have a CNAME record routing the domain to the S3 bucket. That CNAME record must be updated to route queries to the CloudFront distribution domain name. After a CNAME update, propagation can take up to 72 hours, and during propagation some requests go to S3 and others go to CloudFront. Route 53 supports either a CNAME or an alias record set.

### Moving a bucket to a different Region

When a bucket moves to a different Region, CloudFront can take up to an hour to update its records. Consider the case where you use a CloudFront origin access identity (OAI) to restrict access to the bucket and the bucket is moved to an S3 Region that requires Signature Version 4. CloudFront uses the Region to calculate the signature when using OAIs, so updating the distribution forces CloudFront to immediately check the bucket's Region.

## S3 Object Lambda Access Points

Amazon S3 automatically generates a unique alias when an Object Lambda Access Point is created. This alias can be used instead of a bucket name as a CloudFront origin. Origin access control must be used when an Object Lambda Access Point is the CloudFront origin. CloudFront treats an Object Lambda Access Point origin the same as a standard S3 bucket origin.

When using S3 Object Lambda as an origin, four permissions must be configured: Object Lambda Access Point, S3 Access Point, S3 bucket, and Lambda function.

## S3 Access Points

Amazon S3 automatically generates a unique alias for an S3 Access Point. This alias can be used instead of a bucket name as a CloudFront origin. Origin access control must be used when an S3 Access Point is the CloudFront origin. CloudFront treats an S3 Access Point origin the same as a standard S3 bucket origin.

## S3 Multi-Region Access Points

An S3 Multi-Region Access Point can be used as a CloudFront origin. S3 Multi-Region Access Points route requests to the closest bucket based on network latency. For a Multi-Region Access Point origin, the origin domain name is the access point hostname.

## S3 website endpoints

An S3 bucket configured as a website endpoint can be used as a custom origin. For a website endpoint origin, you enter the S3 static website hosting endpoint of the bucket. With the website endpoint format, you can use S3 redirects and S3 custom error documents. When creating a distribution via the API with a website-endpoint bucket, you must use CustomOriginConfig.

## Application Load Balancers

CloudFront can route traffic to both internal and internet-facing Application Load Balancers. An internet-facing load balancer has a publicly resolvable DNS name. Internal ALBs in private subnets can be used with CloudFront via VPC origins.

## Network Load Balancers

CloudFront can be used with both internal and internet-facing Network Load Balancers. Internal NLBs in private subnets can be used with CloudFront via VPC origins.

## EC2 instances

Internal EC2 instances in private subnets can be used with CloudFront via VPC origins.

## Lambda function URLs

A Lambda function URL is a dedicated HTTPS endpoint for a Lambda function. The full domain name of the Lambda function URL is specified as the origin domain. The function URL is invoked directly without API Gateway or an Application Load Balancer. The Lambda function URL must be publicly accessible when used as a CloudFront origin.

If you use origin access control (OAC) with the Lambda function URL, the function URL AuthType must be AWS_IAM, and the resource-based policy must allow lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl and lambda:InvokeFunction.

If you do not use OAC with the Lambda function URL, AuthType can be NONE with lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl allowed in a resource-based policy. In that case, a custom origin header plus function code can ensure users access the application only through CloudFront.

## Lambda Web Functions

A Lambda Web Function is a web application on Lambda that provides its own HTTPS endpoint, and it can be used as a CloudFront origin. The hostname of the Lambda Web Function endpoint is specified as the origin domain. Regional endpoints have hostnames ending in .lambda-web.AWS-Region.on.aws, and global endpoints have hostnames ending in .lambda-web.global.on.aws.

You use OAC with a Lambda Web Function. With OAC, the endpoint auth type must be IamAuth, and the resource-based policy must allow lambda:InvokeWebFunctionEndpoint. CloudFront signs requests to regional endpoints with SigV4 and requests to global endpoints with SigV4a.

## Custom origins

A custom origin is an HTTP(S) web server with a publicly resolvable DNS name. An S3 website endpoint origin is considered a custom origin, and API Gateway can also be used as a custom origin for CloudFront. Most CloudFront features are supported with custom origins except private content. For CloudFront to access a custom origin, the origin must remain publicly accessible. Servers behind a custom origin should serve the same content.

## Origin groups

An origin group allows configuring origin failover with a primary and a secondary origin. CloudFront automatically switches to the second origin when the primary returns specific HTTP failure status codes.

# Choosing and configuring a CloudFront origin

## Before you begin

Complete the following prerequisites before the steps that need them.

- **Amazon S3 bucket** holding the objects to deliver, with a DNS-compliant name. The bucket name must conform to DNS naming requirements to work with CloudFront.
- **S3 Object Lambda Access Point**, which provides the alias used as the origin. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/olap-create.html
- **Amazon S3 Access Point**, which provides the alias used as the origin. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/creating-access-points.html
- **AWS Lambda function** used by the Object Lambda Access Point.
- **CloudFront origin access control**, required for Object Lambda and S3 Access Point origins. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html

## Overview of origins

When you create a distribution, you specify the origin where CloudFront sends requests for files. CloudFront supports several kinds of origins, including S3 buckets, MediaStore containers, MediaPackage channels, Application Load Balancers, and Lambda function URLs. CloudFront automatically configures most distribution settings based on the content origin type. CloudFront Functions or Lambda@Edge can route requests to different origins based on viewer location, request headers, or query string parameters.

An Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer, or EC2 instance in a private subnet can be used as a VPC origin. Because it is a VPC origin, it prevents the application from being accessible on the public internet.

## Amazon S3 bucket origins

Using an existing S3 bucket as a CloudFront origin does not change the bucket. You incur regular Amazon S3 charges for storing objects in the bucket. CloudFront data transfer costs less than S3 data transfer at higher usage, and downloads are faster with CloudFront than with S3 alone.

The recommended S3 origin format is bucket-name.s3.region.amazonaws.com. Only with this format does CloudFront communicate with the bucket using SSL/TLS. Only with this format can origin access control require viewers to use CloudFront URLs rather than S3 URLs. Only with this format can you update bucket content by sending POST and PUT requests to CloudFront. You should not specify the S3 origin using path style or an S3 CNAME.

CloudFront supports S3 origins in any storage class, including S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which does not impact the performance or functionality of a distribution. For CloudFront to respect S3 CORS settings, CloudFront must forward the Origin header to S3.

### Adding CloudFront to a bucket already served by your own domain

When you add CloudFront to an existing bucket, you first create a distribution with the S3 bucket specified as the origin server. Only after that happens do you update the CNAME record, so this order must be kept. CloudFront can be added to a bucket already served via your own domain name with no disruption, but only when two conditions hold: the DNS provider has a CNAME record routing the domain to the S3 bucket (which S3 CNAMEs need in order to work), and that CNAME record is then updated to route queries to the CloudFront distribution domain name. After a CNAME update, propagation can take up to 72 hours. That delay is enough for a mixed state: during propagation, some requests go to S3 and others go to CloudFront. Route 53 supports either a CNAME or an alias record set.

### Moving a bucket to a different Region

When a bucket moves to a different Region, CloudFront can take up to an hour to update its records. This applies only when you use a CloudFront origin access identity (OAI) to restrict access to the bucket and the bucket is moved to an S3 Region that requires Signature Version 4. The delay arises because CloudFront uses the Region to calculate the signature when using OAIs. Updating the distribution forces CloudFront to immediately check the bucket's Region.

## S3 Object Lambda Access Point origins

Amazon S3 automatically generates a unique alias when an Object Lambda Access Point is created. You can use this alias instead of a bucket name as a CloudFront origin. Origin access control must be used with this origin, and CloudFront treats it the same as a standard S3 bucket origin. Four permissions must be configured when using S3 Object Lambda as an origin: the Object Lambda Access Point, the S3 Access Point, the S3 bucket, and the Lambda function.

## S3 Access Point origins

Amazon S3 automatically generates a unique alias for an S3 Access Point. You can use this alias instead of a bucket name as a CloudFront origin. Origin access control must be used when an S3 Access Point is the origin, and CloudFront treats it the same as a standard S3 bucket origin.

## S3 Multi-Region Access Point origins

An S3 Multi-Region Access Point can be used as a CloudFront origin. These access points route requests to the closest bucket based on network latency. For this origin, the origin domain name is the access point hostname.

## S3 website endpoint origins

An S3 bucket configured as a website endpoint can be used as a custom origin, and it is considered a custom origin. You enter the S3 static website hosting endpoint of the bucket. Only with this website endpoint format can you use S3 redirects and S3 custom error documents. Because the bucket is a website endpoint, when you create a distribution via the API you must use CustomOriginConfig.

## Application Load Balancer and Network Load Balancer origins

CloudFront can route traffic to both internal and internet-facing Application Load Balancers. An internet-facing load balancer has a publicly resolvable DNS name. Internal ALBs in private subnets can be used with CloudFront via VPC origins, which prevents the application from being accessible on the public internet.

CloudFront can also be used with both internal and internet-facing Network Load Balancers. Internal NLBs in private subnets can be used with CloudFront via VPC origins.

## Lambda function URL origins

A Lambda function URL is a dedicated HTTPS endpoint for a Lambda function. You specify the full domain name of the function URL as the origin domain. The function URL must be publicly accessible when used as a CloudFront origin. It is invoked directly, without API Gateway or an Application Load Balancer.

If you use origin access control (OAC) with the function URL, the AuthType must be AWS_IAM, and the resource-based policy must allow lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl and lambda:InvokeFunction. If you do not use OAC, then AuthType can be NONE with lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl allowed in a resource-based policy; this applies only when OAC is not used. A custom origin header plus function code can ensure users access the application only through CloudFront.

## Lambda Web Function origins

A Lambda Web Function is a web application on Lambda that provides its own HTTPS endpoint, and it can be used as a CloudFront origin. You specify the hostname of the endpoint as the origin domain. Regional endpoints have hostnames ending in .lambda-web.AWS-Region.on.aws, and global endpoints have hostnames ending in .lambda-web.global.on.aws.

You use OAC with a Lambda Web Function. The endpoint auth type of IamAuth applies only when you use OAC, and the resource-based policy must allow lambda:InvokeWebFunctionEndpoint. CloudFront signs requests to regional endpoints with SigV4 and requests to global endpoints with SigV4a.

## Custom origins

A custom origin is an HTTP(S) web server with a publicly resolvable DNS name. Most CloudFront features are supported with custom origins except private content. Because it is a custom origin, it must remain publicly accessible for CloudFront to access it. Internal EC2 instances in private subnets can be used with CloudFront via VPC origins. API Gateway can be used as a custom origin for CloudFront. Servers behind a custom origin should serve the same content.

CloudFront uses UTC for signed URLs, signed cookies, logs, and reports.

## Origin failover

An origin group allows configuring origin failover with a primary and a secondary origin. CloudFront automatically switches to the second origin when the primary returns specific HTTP failure status codes.

# Choosing and configuring CloudFront origins

## Overview

When you create a distribution, you specify the origin where CloudFront sends requests for files. CloudFront supports several kinds of origins, including S3 buckets, MediaStore containers, MediaPackage channels, Application Load Balancers, and Lambda function URLs. It automatically configures most distribution settings based on the content origin type. API Gateway can also be used as a custom origin.

An Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer, or EC2 instance in a private subnet can be used as a VPC origin. VPC origins prevent the application from being accessible on the public internet. CloudFront Functions or Lambda@Edge can route requests to different origins based on viewer location, request headers, or query string parameters.

## Amazon S3 origins

Using an existing S3 bucket as a CloudFront origin does not change the bucket, and you continue to incur regular Amazon S3 charges for storing objects in it. The bucket name must conform to DNS naming requirements to work with CloudFront.

The recommended S3 origin format is `bucket-name.s3.region.amazonaws.com`. With this format:
- CloudFront can communicate with the bucket using SSL/TLS.
- Origin access control can require viewers to use CloudFront URLs rather than S3 URLs.
- You can update bucket content by sending POST and PUT requests to CloudFront.

You should not specify the S3 origin using path style or an S3 CNAME.

CloudFront supports S3 origins in any storage class, including S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which does not impact the performance or functionality of a distribution. CloudFront data transfer costs less than S3 data transfer at higher usage, and downloads are faster with CloudFront than with S3 alone. To respect S3 CORS settings, CloudFront must forward the Origin header to S3.

### S3 Object Lambda Access Points

Amazon S3 automatically generates a unique alias when an Object Lambda Access Point is created. You can use this alias instead of a bucket name as a CloudFront origin. When an Object Lambda Access Point is the origin, origin access control must be used. CloudFront treats it the same as a standard S3 bucket origin. Four permissions must be configured when using S3 Object Lambda as an origin: Object Lambda Access Point, S3 Access Point, S3 bucket, and Lambda function.

### S3 Access Points

Amazon S3 automatically generates a unique alias for an S3 Access Point. You can use this alias instead of a bucket name as a CloudFront origin. When an S3 Access Point is the origin, origin access control must be used. CloudFront treats it the same as a standard S3 bucket origin.

### S3 Multi-Region Access Points

An S3 Multi-Region Access Point can be used as a CloudFront origin. These access points route requests to the closest bucket based on network latency. For this origin, the origin domain name is the access point hostname.

### S3 website endpoints

An S3 bucket configured as a website endpoint can be used as a custom origin. For this origin, you enter the S3 static website hosting endpoint of the bucket. With the website endpoint format, you can use S3 redirects and S3 custom error documents. If you create a distribution via the API with a website-endpoint bucket, you must use CustomOriginConfig.

### Adding CloudFront to an existing bucket

CloudFront can be added to a bucket already served via your own domain name with no disruption. When you add it, a distribution is created with the S3 bucket specified as origin server. For S3 CNAMEs to work, the DNS provider must have a CNAME record routing the domain to the S3 bucket. That record must then be updated to route queries to the CloudFront distribution domain name. After a CNAME update, propagation can take up to 72 hours, and during propagation some requests go to S3 and others go to CloudFront. Route 53 supports either a CNAME or an alias record set.

### Moving a bucket to a different Region

When a bucket moves to a different Region, CloudFront can take up to an hour to update its records. This matters if you use a CloudFront origin access identity (OAI) to restrict access to the bucket and the bucket is moved to an S3 Region that requires Signature Version 4. In that case, because CloudFront uses the Region to calculate the signature when using OAIs, updating the distribution forces CloudFront to immediately check the bucket's Region.

## Load balancer and EC2 origins

CloudFront can route traffic to both internal and internet-facing Application Load Balancers. An internet-facing load balancer has a publicly resolvable DNS name. Internal ALBs in private subnets can be used with CloudFront via VPC origins. CloudFront can likewise be used with both internal and internet-facing Network Load Balancers, and internal NLBs in private subnets can be used via VPC origins. Internal EC2 instances in private subnets can also be used via VPC origins.

## Lambda function URL origins

A Lambda function URL is a dedicated HTTPS endpoint for a Lambda function. You specify its full domain name as the origin domain. The function URL must be publicly accessible when used as a CloudFront origin. It is invoked directly, without API Gateway or an Application Load Balancer.

- **With origin access control (OAC):** the function URL AuthType must be AWS_IAM, and the resource-based policy must allow lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl and lambda:InvokeFunction.
- **Without OAC:** AuthType can be NONE, with lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl allowed in a resource-based policy. A custom origin header plus function code can then ensure users access the application only through CloudFront.

## Lambda Web Function origins

A Lambda Web Function is a web application on Lambda that provides its own HTTPS endpoint, and it can be used as a CloudFront origin. You specify the hostname of the endpoint as the origin domain. Regional endpoints have hostnames ending in `.lambda-web.AWS-Region.on.aws`, and global endpoints have hostnames ending in `.lambda-web.global.on.aws`.

When you use OAC with a Lambda Web Function, the endpoint auth type must be IamAuth, and the resource-based policy must allow lambda:InvokeWebFunctionEndpoint. CloudFront signs requests to regional endpoints with SigV4 and requests to global endpoints with SigV4a.

## Custom origins

A custom origin is an HTTP(S) web server with a publicly resolvable DNS name. An S3 website endpoint origin is considered a custom origin. Most CloudFront features are supported with custom origins except private content. For CloudFront to access a custom origin, the origin must remain publicly accessible. Servers behind a custom origin should serve the same content.

## Origin failover and time handling

An origin group allows configuring origin failover with a primary and a secondary origin. CloudFront automatically switches to the second origin when the primary returns specific HTTP failure status codes. CloudFront uses UTC for signed URLs, signed cookies, logs, and reports.

# Choosing and configuring a CloudFront origin

## Before you begin

Complete the following prerequisites before the steps that need them. Where a prerequisite says "steps on this page," the steps appear in the sections below.

- **Amazon S3 bucket with a DNS-compliant name.** The bucket backs the access points and holds the objects. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucketnamingrules.html
- **Amazon S3 Access Point.** Create it either as the supporting access point for Object Lambda or for direct origin use. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/creating-access-points.html
- **AWS Lambda function** used by the Object Lambda Access Point.
- **Object Lambda Access Point**, with its generated alias, to use as the origin. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/olap-create.html
- **Origin access control (OAC) for the CloudFront distribution.** It is required when you use an Object Lambda Access Point or S3 Access Point origin. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html
- **Object Lambda Access Point policy** allowing CloudFront service principal access (steps on this page).
- **S3 Access Point policy** allowing CloudFront service principal access (steps on this page).
- **S3 bucket policy** granting access for the account/CloudFront, delegating to access points (steps on this page).
- **Lambda function resource-based policy** allowing cloudfront.amazonaws.com to invoke the function (steps on this page).

## Origins in general

When you create a distribution, you specify the origin where CloudFront sends requests for files. CloudFront supports several kinds of origins, including S3 buckets, MediaStore containers, MediaPackage channels, Application Load Balancers, and Lambda function URLs. CloudFront automatically configures most distribution settings based on the content origin type. CloudFront Functions or Lambda@Edge can route requests to different origins based on viewer location, request headers, or query string parameters.

An Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer, or EC2 instance in a private subnet can be used as a VPC origin. Because it is a VPC origin, the application is not accessible on the public internet.

## Amazon S3 bucket origins

Using an existing S3 bucket as a CloudFront origin does not change the bucket. You incur regular Amazon S3 charges for storing objects in the bucket. The bucket name must conform to DNS naming requirements to work with CloudFront. CloudFront supports S3 origins in any storage class, including S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which does not impact the performance or functionality of a distribution.

The recommended S3 origin format is bucket-name.s3.region.amazonaws.com. Only with this format do the following hold: CloudFront can communicate with the bucket using SSL/TLS; origin access control can require viewers to use CloudFront URLs rather than S3 URLs; and you can update bucket content by sending POST and PUT requests to CloudFront. You should not specify the S3 origin using path style or an S3 CNAME.

Putting CloudFront in front of S3 has benefits. CloudFront data transfer costs less than S3 data transfer at higher usage, and downloads are faster with CloudFront than with S3 alone. To respect S3 CORS settings, CloudFront must forward the Origin header to S3.

### Adding CloudFront to a bucket already served by your own domain

CloudFront can be added to a bucket already served via your own domain name with no disruption, but only if the DNS provider has a CNAME record routing the domain to the S3 bucket (which S3 CNAMEs require) and that CNAME record is updated to route queries to the CloudFront distribution domain name. The order matters: first create a distribution with the S3 bucket specified as the origin server, and only then update the CNAME record. After a CNAME update, propagation can take up to 72 hours, and during propagation some requests go to S3 and others go to CloudFront. Route 53 supports either a CNAME or an alias record set.

### Moving a bucket to a different Region

When a bucket moves to a different Region, CloudFront can take up to an hour to update its records. This applies only when you use a CloudFront origin access identity (OAI) to restrict access to the bucket and the bucket is moved to an S3 Region that requires Signature Version 4. The delay arises because CloudFront uses the Region to calculate the signature when using OAIs. Updating the distribution forces CloudFront to immediately check the bucket's Region.

## S3 Object Lambda Access Point origins

Amazon S3 automatically generates a unique alias when an Object Lambda Access Point is created. You can use this alias instead of a bucket name as a CloudFront origin. Origin access control must be used when an Object Lambda Access Point is the CloudFront origin. CloudFront treats an Object Lambda Access Point origin the same as a standard S3 bucket origin.

Four permissions must be configured when using S3 Object Lambda as an origin: Object Lambda Access Point, S3 Access Point, S3 bucket, and Lambda function. These correspond to the policies listed in the prerequisites.

## S3 Access Point origins

Amazon S3 automatically generates a unique alias for an S3 Access Point. You can use this alias instead of a bucket name as a CloudFront origin. Origin access control must be used when an S3 Access Point is the CloudFront origin. CloudFront treats an S3 Access Point origin the same as a standard S3 bucket origin.

## S3 Multi-Region Access Point origins

An S3 Multi-Region Access Point can be used as a CloudFront origin. Multi-Region Access Points route requests to the closest bucket based on network latency. For this origin, the origin domain name is the access point hostname.

## S3 website endpoint origins

An S3 bucket configured as a website endpoint can be used as a custom origin. You enter the S3 static website hosting endpoint of the bucket. Only when you enter that website endpoint can you use S3 redirects and S3 custom error documents. Because the bucket is a website-endpoint origin, when you create a distribution via the API you must use CustomOriginConfig.

## Custom origins

A custom origin is an HTTP(S) web server with a publicly resolvable DNS name. An S3 website endpoint origin is considered a custom origin. Most CloudFront features are supported with custom origins except private content. Because it is a custom origin, for CloudFront to access it the origin must remain publicly accessible. Servers behind a custom origin should serve the same content. CloudFront uses UTC for signed URLs, signed cookies, logs, and reports.

An origin group allows you to configure origin failover with a primary and a secondary origin. CloudFront automatically switches to the second origin when the primary returns specific HTTP failure status codes. API Gateway can also be used as a custom origin for CloudFront.

### Application Load Balancers

CloudFront can route traffic to both internal and internet-facing Application Load Balancers. An internet-facing load balancer has a publicly resolvable DNS name. Internal ALBs in private subnets can be used with CloudFront via VPC origins, which prevents the application from being accessible on the public internet.

### Network Load Balancers

CloudFront can be used with both internal and internet-facing Network Load Balancers. Internal NLBs in private subnets can be used with CloudFront via VPC origins.

### EC2 instances

Internal EC2 instances in private subnets can be used with CloudFront via VPC origins.

## Lambda function URL origins

A Lambda function URL is a dedicated HTTPS endpoint for a Lambda function. The function URL is invoked directly, without API Gateway or an Application Load Balancer. You specify the full domain name of the function URL as the origin domain. The function URL must be publicly accessible when used as a CloudFront origin.

If you use origin access control (OAC) with the function URL, then the function URL AuthType must be AWS_IAM, and the resource-based policy must allow lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl and lambda:InvokeFunction. These requirements apply only when you use OAC.

If you do not use OAC with the function URL, AuthType can be NONE with lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl allowed in a resource-based policy. This applies only when OAC is not used. In that case, a custom origin header plus function code can ensure users access the application only through CloudFront.

## Lambda Web Function origins

A Lambda Web Function is a web application on Lambda that provides its own HTTPS endpoint, and it can be used as a CloudFront origin. You specify the hostname of the endpoint as the origin domain. Regional endpoints have hostnames ending in .lambda-web.AWS-Region.on.aws, and global endpoints have hostnames ending in .lambda-web.global.on.aws.

You use OAC with a Lambda Web Function. With OAC, the endpoint auth type must be IamAuth, and the resource-based policy must allow lambda:InvokeWebFunctionEndpoint. CloudFront signs requests to regional endpoints with SigV4 and requests to global endpoints with SigV4a.
